nodes.body:
**Upgrade regression: directories created by earlier releases are now rejected.**

Before this PR, the upload, Hub import and project import paths created the attachment root and shard directories with `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })` and no `mode`. Their permissions therefore came from the process umask. With a group-writable umask such as `002` (the default for user-private-group logins on Debian and Ubuntu), these directories are `0o775`. This line now treats any `0o022` bit on the root or shard as invalid and never repairs it. On an existing installation:

- `createControllerBackup` → `attachmentObjectPath` throws `Unsafe attachment object path` for every existing attachment. Full backups and `--backup-before-migration` stop working.
- Uploads and imports into any existing shard fail with `invalid_request`.

The data directory itself passes, because `privateDirectory` requires it to be `0o700`. Only the attachment subdirectories, which old code never hardened, are affected. That makes this hard to diagnose.

The new tests always create these directories through the new code, or use a `0o755` parent ("retains legacy directory modes"), so this path is untested. Two possible fixes: harden owned legacy root and shard directories once (for example, `fchmod` to `0o700` when the owner matches the current user and there is no symlink), or apply the check only to directories this code creates. Please also add a test with a pre-existing `0o775` root and shard.

Reviewed by: claude-opus-5-5

**Publication now requires read permission on every ancestor up to `/`.**

`syncParents` calls `syncDirectory`, which runs `openSync(path, O_RDONLY)`, on every directory from the shard up to the filesystem root. Opening a directory needs read permission. Path traversal only needs execute permission, and `privateDirectory`/`assertAncestors` do not require ancestors to be readable. So a data directory under an execute-only ancestor fails here. Examples are `WORKTREE_SWITCHER_DATA_DIR=/srv/ws/data` with `/srv` set to `root:root 0711`, or a home directory under a hardened `0711` parent.

The failure happens after `linkSync` has already published the object, so `upload`, Hub import and project import all throw EACCES before SQL runs. Retries take the "existing object" branch and fail in the same `syncParents` call, so the condition is permanent. Before this PR, the same configuration worked. This is not an injected-fault case like the `directory-sync:EACCES` test. It is a deterministic regression for that layout.

Durability only needs fsync on directories whose entries this call (or an interrupted earlier attempt) could have created: the shard, the root, and newly created ancestors up to the first pre-existing private directory. Ancestors above the database private data directory never get new entries from this code. Please limit the walk, or treat EACCES on those outer ancestors as non-fatal.

Safe existing modes remain unchanged; symlink roots/shards, foreign ownership and writable outer ancestors are still rejected without chmod.

Regression tests cover real pre-existing 0775 roots/shards for upload, Hub import, project import and backup, plus unchanged object inode/bytes and rejection without repair of foreign directories and symlink targets. fix — addressed in af34b7b31b843281ee08305bff464045e2a3ce61 (now on the PR branch).

Directory fsync now stops after the shard, object root and its existing parent. The publisher creates only root/shard directories under the already established data directory or backup staging; it never creates outer ancestors. Every publication and deduplication retry synchronizes all three directories, including entries left by an interrupted attempt. Ancestors above this boundary are still checked for unsafe paths/permissions with stat, but never opened for read or synchronized.
